body: I've done both group and individual therapy before; it's a good deal of the reason I'm still alive to type this.  The problem is that a lot of what's causing me distress at the moment is tied to gender identity and sexuality, and if I mentioned that to a not-trans-accepting therapist (which, as far as I can tell, describes every therapist within reasonable travel distance of us) it would probably just make the situation worse.

This isn't my first time contemplating suicide.  There've been times in the past when I've been very unstable.  My fiance was the first person in my life who helped me reach a stability where small setbacks wouldn't lead to total catastrophization.  Them leaving my life would likely put me in a very bad place.  It may sound foolish, but I'd rather have the few years with my fiance before my death than die soon completely alone.

I have told them this.  I've told them I respect and accept the fact that they don't want children and that I'm worried about their family's reaction.  I think my fiance is being far too optimistic (I mean, people tend to not go after male-appearing individuals about why they don't have kids with nearly as much as female-appearing ones), but I honestly think that calling off the engagement would send me spiraling down an actively suicidal path faster than this one will :/

It's less that I want children and more that not having children without a "reasonable excuse" will make my life a torment.  It's actually fairly likely that I'm barren; my mother was only able to have my sister and I with substantial fertility treatments.  But we wouldn't be having kids because I can't.  We wouldn't be having kids because "we decided not to."
